pageCache.pageTitle: Tarnerland Nursery School - Carers and Creators
pageCache.text:
Carers and Creators
(3 - 5 years)
Our over 3s provision at Tarnerland, known as Carers and Creators, marks the final stage of the children's journey before starting school. Our team of two Early Years teachers, four nursery assistants and four additional support workers, supported by our lead teacher, Jan, focuses on learning, independence and increased responsibility. This stage is designed to help children feel confident, capable and ready for what comes next.
The preschool is made up of two thoughtfully designed main rooms. Blue Room offers a focused environment for table-top play and learning, where children can practise early writing, play maths games, build with construction resources or play with our wealth of small-world and role-play sets. Orange Room is dedicated to more messy and creative activities, providing opportunities for open-ended exploration and self-expression with sand, water, paint, playdough, reclaimed materials, and more. In addition, there are two separate smaller spaces used for teaching sessions and a Regulation Station for those children who need moments of calm and quiet.
The daily routine in Carers and Creators has increased structure as the children take part in more adult-led activities. Each day includes a welcoming hello time, dedicated key person group sessions in both the morning and the afternoon and an extended story-time before tea. Key person times are planned by our lead teacher, Jan, and the children are exposed to stories, rhymes, songs, games, discussions and other focused learning tailored to their stage of development.
Outdoor learning plays a central role in our approach. Children spend time in the meadow every morning and afternoon and we run weekly Forest School sessions for all over 3s. Further details can be found on our Meadow and Forest School page for more information.
We maintain strong, long-standing links with local schools and support each child’s transition with care. From learning to manage routines to building social skills and independence, we aim to give every child the best possible start as they prepare to move on from nursery.

pageCache.pageTitle: Tarnerland Nursery School - Lookers and Explorers
pageCache.text:
Lookers and Explorers
(9 months - 2 years)
The baby room at Tarnerland, known as Lookers and Explorers, marks the beginning of many children’s journey through our nursery. Our team of seven nursery assistants, led by room leader Vicky, provides a settled, nurturing environment where babies are supported to explore the world around them in a way that is both secure and stimulating.
We operate a strong key person system, ensuring that each child is cared for by an adult who takes time to understand their individual needs, routines, and preferences. These relationships are central to supporting emotional wellbeing and help babies build confidence from the very beginning.
At this early stage, care and learning go hand in hand. Through age-appropriate experiences and interactions, including sensory exploration, shared play and lots of stories, songs and rhymes, children begin to develop key skills in a way that is responsive to their pace and interests.
We place great importance on working in partnership with the families of these youngest children. Regular communication takes place through conversations at drop-off and collection times, and we share learning and special moments via our online platform, Famly.
Our Lookers and Explorers group provides a gentle and supportive start to nursery life, where children can settle, grow, and begin forming friendships. As they develop, we work carefully to prepare them for a smooth transition into our toddler room.

pageCache.pageTitle: Tarnerland Nursery School - Players and Pretenders
pageCache.text:
Players and Pretenders
(2 - 3 years)
Our Players and Pretenders (toddlers) rooms, are vibrant, engaging spaces where children begin to explore the world with growing curiosity. Our team of nine nursery assistants, including room leader Darcie and deputy room leader Amelia, provide a nurturing and stimulating environment where toddlers begin to take steps towards independence, social skills and emotional resilience.
We focus on supporting children as they develop essential skills around communication and problem-solving, including self-help. Through a variety of play-based experiences such as role-play, small-world play, structured games, creative and tactile exploration and, of course, lots of stories, songs and rhymes, toddlers have the opportunity to express themselves and build confidence.
We recognise that this stage of development can bring challenges, and our team is dedicated to helping each child navigate their emotions with care and understanding. The key person system continues to play a vital role in fostering secure relationships, allowing toddlers to feel supported as they explore new social dynamics and gain confidence in their abilities.
The routine in our Players and Pretenders group includes a mid-day sleep, allowing those children who need it, the opportunity recharge in a quiet, comforting environment. The children spend time in the meadow every morning and afternoon and this period of rest ensures that they have the energy for a full and active day of learning.

The Governing Body
Who are we?
We are volunteers and we come from every section of the community. Tarnerland's governing body is made up of 12 people including staff, parents, local authority and community representatives.
In a nutshell we are here to help the school provide the best possible education for the children.
We support and encourage all aspects of nursery life by acting as a "critical friend". By that we mean we fully support our headteacher, Louise, but also ask important and difficult questions. We are an integral part of life at the school. We celebrate the nursery's many successes and achievements.
Minutes from governing body meetings, including attendance, are available from the school on request and the register of declarations of interests is here;
Declarations of Interest Register March 2026
Ella Turner, Chair of Governors, co-opted govenor, current term 2025 to 2029
Ella is a former primary assistant headteacher and school improvement consultant. She grew up in Hanover in the 1980s and attended Tarnerland herself as a child. She started as a governor when her daughter started nursery in 2006 and has been here ever since.
She loves the nursery’s long tradition of supporting families in the Tarner community and the amazing outdoor space. She feels privileged to spend time with the staff and children and see the hard work that goes into making Tarnerland such a special place. She has been Chair of Governors since 2021.
Chris Chapman, Vice Chair of Governors and Chair of Health, Safety and Wellbeing Committee, co-opted govenor, current term 2022 to 2026
Chris joined the Governing Body as a parent governor in 2010, when his eldest son attended the nursery. Since then, both of his younger children have also enjoyed their time at Tarnerland, moving right through from the baby room to the over-3s.
Chris runs a small accountancy practice in Brighton and particularly enjoys contributing to the finance committee and budget-monitoring meetings.
Chris loves being a governor at Tarnerland and is committed to supporting Louise, Jackie, and the whole fantastic staff team in achieving the best possible outcomes for all the children in their care.
Penny Dunne, Chair of Finance Committee, co-opted govenor, current term 2023 to 2027
Penny has lived in the Tarnerland area with her husband since 1968, raising two daughters who both attended the nursery school. She joined the management committee in 1973, the forerunner of today's governors, and has served ever since.
Active in community politics during the 1970s, Penny helped establish the Royal Spa Nursery School and the Hanover Community Association. She later trained as a solicitor, practising family law from 1980 to 2005, with a particular focus on public law child care work. She also co-founded a family mediation service in 1998 and worked as a mediator until 2018.
Now retired, Penny enjoys time with her grandchildren and values her long connection with Tarnerland, which has allowed her to continue to support the development of care and education for the under 5s.
Joanne Marron, co-opted govenor, current term 2024 to 2028
Joanne is a teacher at Westdene Primary School in Brighton where she has worked for over 10 years. Joanne has built up a wealth of experience teaching in both nursery and reception and has led the foundation stage and been a member of senior leadership for over 5 years.
As a practitioner, leader and school governor, Joanne believes excellent Early Years teaching and pedagogy can impact positively on all children's futures.
Joanne is currently seconded as the Early Years Specialist for the Education and Standards Team at Brighton and Hove City Council. In this post, she offers support, consultancy and guidance to schools across the city. Joanne also leads two Early Years cluster groups where she facilitates practitioners connecting and sharing best practice.
Joanne is excited to join the governance team at Tarnerland and make a positive contribution to such a beautiful and vibrant setting where Early Years is so valued.
Samira Vance, co-opted governor, current term 2024 to 2028
Samira started her teaching career in Brighton and Hove with a PGCE in Primary Education at Brighton University after doing a BA in Law and Human Rights at the University of Essex.
Samira has taught at Elm Grove Primary School (where she was also the English as an Additional Language Coordinator) and then moved to Bangkok, Thailand where she taught across four key stages, including Early Years, in British international schools.
Most recently, Samira was the Director of Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) at King's College International School Bangkok and is the founder of the Thailand DEI Hub.
Samira has also been providing training and consultancy to senior leaders and safeguarding leads. She is particularly interested in the safeguarding of minoritised groups, community engagement, curriculum development and, professional development and wellbeing of staff.
Samira is excited to join the board and looks forward to working with governors in such a wonderful setting.
Tracey Paul, co-opted governor current term 2025 to 2029
At the beginning of her career, Tracey worked as an assistant to a financial planner in a well-known accountancy firm. She then embarked on a 32-year career in a global company as a Business Analyst and Project Manager, including gaining a diploma in Business Management.
Having an interest in education led Tracey to a role as a clerk to governors in a local primary school for a period. She moved on from this to governor at Tarnerland where she hopes to use her experience to contribute usefully to the governing body, as well as increasing her understanding of the structure, compliance, policies and best practice adopted in an educational setting.
Louise Collings, headteacher governor
Louise joined Tarnerland as headteacher in September 2023. Her background is originally as a teacher in primary schools where the majority of her experience was within Early Years and where she progressed to EYFS lead and then deputy headteacher. Following this, Louise spent 10 years working as a specialist teacher for the Brighton and Hove Inclusion Support Service Early Years team, leading this team as senior teacher for 2 years. Louise is committed to improving children's outcomes and feels privileged to be playing such an important part in this vibrant community.
Jackie Poulton, co-opted governor, current term 2024 to 2028
Jackie has been the nursery manager at Tarnerland since 2016 but has worked in childcare for 31 years, starting as a trainee practitioner. She spent 13 of those years managing a team and leading practice for Early Years in Children's Centres in East Sussex, working with families from pregnancy, supporting positive parenting in stay and play groups, delivering training to staff and families regarding accidents in the home for CAPT and promoting and supporting positive feeding (breast and bottle) for UNICEF.
Darcie Watts, staff governor, current term 2025 to 2029
Darcie has worked at Tarnerland for 4 years. She holds a CACHE Level 3 qualification in Early Years Education, alongside a Bachelor of Arts in Childhood and Youth Studies. She has over 9 years of experience working with children across a range of settings, developing a strong understanding of child development and individual needs. In addition to her work in education, Darcie has 9 years of experience working in social care, supporting children and adults with disabilities.
As a staff governor, Darcie brings valuable frontline insight into daily practice, safeguarding and inclusion, using her professional experience to contribute meaningfully to discussions.
Vahsti Hale, parent governor, current term 2025 to 2029
After first moving to Brighton to study at the University of Sussex in 1997, Vahsti returned to the city in 2018 and now has a daughter attending Tarnerland. Vahsti is a social and health researcher specialising in policy and communications. She works with public and voluntary sector organisations to deliver research that informs service improvement and drives evidence-based policy change. With a particular interest in behavioural health and a specialism in inclusive research practice, she is passionate about improving outcomes across education, health, and wider public services.
Alongside her professional work, Vashti is a non-executive director of Healthwatch Brighton and Hove CIC and runs Hove Netball. As a parent governor, she hopes to draw on her experience in research and community engagement to support Tarnerland's commitment to inclusion, health and wellbeing, and giving every child the best possible start.

Welcome
Tarnerland Nursery School is an outstanding education and childcare provider for children from 3 months to 5 years of age. It is funded by the Brighton and Hove Local Education Authority in partnership with the council’s Children’s and Family Services and is closely linked to the Tarner Family Hub. The nursery has a long established reputation of providing quality early education and care which we are delighted to maintain, reflected again in our April 2026 Ofsted report;
Tarnerland Nursery School - Ofsted - Find an Inspection Report
This is particularly pleasing because, as a maintained nursery school, we have to meet the strict criteria of a full school inspection. Our success is due to the outstanding practice of our well-qualified, experienced and committed staff team. The Headteacher has a long career in teaching with significant experience around inclusion and her deputy, the Nursery Manager, has a successful background in children’s services.
At our nursery school, we believe that every child and family deserves to feel safe, valued, welcomed and included. We are committed to the vision of the School of Sanctuary movement, creating a place where children and families seeking sanctuary, alongside all members of our community, experience a sense of belonging and respect. We celebrate diversity and recognise the richness that different cultures, languages, experiences and identities bring to our nursery.
Welcome to Tarnerland!

pageCache.pageTitle: Tarnerland Nursery School - The Meadow and Forest School
pageCache.text:
The Meadow and Forest School
At Tarnerland Nursery School, outdoor learning is at the heart of our approach. Opened in 1933 as one of the country’s first ‘open air nurseries’, we are proud to continue this legacy today. Our large garden, known as 'the meadow', remains a much-loved part of nursery life and provides a rich, natural environment for play, exploration and learning.
Shaded by mature trees and alive with seasonal changes, the meadow offers children space to run, climb, dig and discover. Carefully designed areas within the meadow invite a wide range of opportunities — from messy play in the mud kitchen to quiet storytelling around the fire to swinging on the monkey bars.
Our nursery groups take turns using the meadow every morning and afternoon, ensuring all children have daily opportunities to enjoy the fresh air and freedom of this special space.
Forest School sessions also take place here each week for our over 3s. Led by our trained Forest School Leader, Jan, these sessions support children’s physical, social and emotional development through hands-on experiences in nature. From learning to use tools safely to making shelters and toasting snacks over a fire, Forest School gives children the chance to take supported risks, solve problems, and connect with the natural world.
The meadow and Forest School remain central to what makes Tarnerland unique — offering children the space to thrive, learn and grow within a beautiful, ever-changing outdoor environment.

Admissions
If you would like your child to attend Tarnerland Nursery School, please READ THIS PAGE before completing the enquiry form below. We aim to respond to any enquiries within a week.
We only offer fixed attendance patterns at Tarnerland Nursery School, with no bespoke options available. This is to enable us to offer the government funding to as many children as possible over 47.5 weeks of the year. This means that children will be eligible for 12 or 24 hours, all year round, instead of the 15 or 30 hours, term-time only. Attendance options for 24 hour children are limited to;
(2 x 10 hour days + 1 x 4 hour morning or afternoon)
Either beginning of the week (Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday morning) or end of the week (Wednesday afternoon, Thursday, Friday).
Either beginning of the week (Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday) or end of the week (Wednesday, Thursday, Friday).
Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday (Wednesdays NOT available on this pattern).
Children only eligible for 12 hours can attend on one of two attendance patterns;
Mon and Tues mornings (8.30am to 12.30pm)
and Thurs afternoons (1pm to 5pm)
Tues afternoons (1pm to 5pm) and
Thurs and Fri mornings (8.30am to 12.30pm)
Alternatively, 12 hour children can 'top-up' to one of the 24 hour attendance patterns above.
